cases.input: Explain the difference between TCP and UDP.
cases.output_a: TCP is connection-oriented: it sets up a connection and guarantees ordered, reliable delivery with retransmission. UDP is connectionless and sends datagrams without delivery guarantees or ordering, so it is faster and used for streaming, DNS and games.
cases.output_b: TCP is connection-oriented: it performs a handshake, then guarantees ordered, reliable delivery using acknowledgements and retransmission, plus flow and congestion control. UDP is connectionless: it sends independent datagrams with no handshake, ordering or delivery guarantee, which makes it lighter and lower-latency. Use TCP for web pages and file transfer; use UDP for DNS, voice/video streaming and games.

cases.input: Explain what a hash map is in two sentences.
cases.system_prompt: Answer in at most two sentences.
cases.output_a: A hash map stores key-value pairs and uses a hash function to turn each key into an array index. Lookups, inserts and deletes take O(1) time on average. Collisions are handled with chaining or open addressing. They are used in caches, sets and databases.
cases.output_b: A hash map stores key-value pairs and uses a hash function to turn each key into an index into an array, so lookups, inserts and deletes take O(1) time on average. Collisions, where two keys map to the same index, are handled with techniques like chaining or open addressing.
cases.gold_note: both correct; A breaks the 2-sentence limit
